claim: Trigger Once only stops a sprite, wall or sector being set off directly (pushed, shot, touched, entered); a message arriving on its rx channel is obeyed every time. And a state command that names the state the object is already in sends nothing, so a toggle driven by explicit ON reports only its first change.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/triggers.cpp:1888-1893 trTriggerSprite checks and sets isTriggered/triggerOnce (1843 sectors, 1867 walls); trMessageSprite at triggers.cpp:1956 does not look at it
NBlood/source/blood/src/triggers.cpp:85-88 SetSpriteState returns 0 without sending when state already equals nState
Functions: triggers.cpp:1841 trTriggerSector, :1865 trTriggerWall, :1889 trTriggerSprite, :1956 trMessageSprite (also :1913 trMessageSector, :1934 trMessageWall), :85 SetSpriteState.
use: To latch something that is also wired, do not rely on Trigger Once: send it an explicit ON (command 1), or put a counter/once-only relay in front of it.

checked.how: triggers.cpp:1841-1845 trTriggerSector, :1865-1869 trTriggerWall, :1889-1893 trTriggerSprite: each acts only if !locked && !isTriggered and sets isTriggered when triggerOnce; :1956-1977 trMessageSprite tests only locked, then OperateSprite (trMessageSector :1913, trMessageWall :1934 likewise). :85-88 SetSpriteState returns 0 when busy is settled and state == nState, before any evSend.
